purpose: Structure buyer feedback so it becomes a machine-actionable task, not an email in an inbox. Every piece of feedback enters the evidence loop.
constitutional_basis: Article XXXV — closed-loop epistemic control. Buyer feedback is the 'reality' input to the loop. Without it, the loop is software-only.

feedback_categories.description: Buyer asks a technical question about the package (e.g., 'How did you derive K_p=0.020?')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Generate a detailed technical response. If the question reveals a gap in the TTP, create a TTP update task. If the question reveals a falsifiable claim, add it to the test queue.
examples: How does the controller behave if the lesion decay rate is 10x faster than modelled?
What is the implications of the simulator's falsification of the strict dual-invariant claim?
Can the predictor be replaced with a Kalman filter?

feedback_categories.description: Buyer challenges an economic assumption (e.g., 'Our revision cost is actually $15K, not $30K')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Update COMMERCIAL_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.json with buyer-verified value. Re-run sensitivity analysis. If the package's value proposition is significantly weakened, escalate to TTP revision.
examples: Our average revision cost is $15K, not $30K — your economic model is too optimistic
Our obstruction rate is 15%, not 30% — your market size is overstated
We use prophylactic replacement at 5 years, so your 'avoided revision' framing doesn't apply

feedback_categories.description: Buyer suggests a design change (e.g., 'Use 6 segments instead of 4')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Add to design_revision_queue.json. If suggestion aligns with simulator's identified design limit (e.g., 4 segments insufficient), prioritize for next iteration.
examples: Use 6 segments instead of 4 — gives more redundancy
Add an accumulator buffer to handle pulsation peaks
Replace MEMS valve with shape-memory alloy — simpler

feedback_categories.description: Buyer expresses willingness to evaluate a prototype (the gold signal — 'send me the prototype')
feedback_categories.machine_action: This is the highest-priority signal. Immediately package the EXTERNAL_VALIDATION_HANDOFF folder, ship to buyer, begin formal validation engagement. Update state machine: PROTOTYPE_READY → PILOT.
examples: Send us the V0 bench prototype spec — we'll build it in our lab
We want to run the simulator on our hardware first, then decide
Send the V1 implantable prototype — we have animal model ready

feedback_categories.description: Buyer's regulatory team provides insight (e.g., 'FDA would require PCCP for the predictive algorithm')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Update TTP element 11 (regulatory map). Add to regulatory_questions.json. May trigger pre-submission meeting planning.
examples: FDA Q-Submission program would be ideal for early feedback on this novel approach
PCCP (Predetermined Change Control Plan) likely required for the predictive algorithm
Animal model requirement is 6 months chronic, not 3 months acute

feedback_categories.description: Buyer's IP counsel provides FTO insight (e.g., 'US12636471 may cover your predictive redistribution')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Update TTP element 10 (IP dossier). Add to IP_questions.json. May trigger design-around exploration.
examples: US12636471 (2026 CSF metering) claims may cover your redistribution algorithm
Your dual-invariant formulation is similar to a 1998 aerospace patent — need to check
The enzyme cocktail combination may be patentable as a composition of matter

feedback_categories.description: Buyer explicitly rejects the package (e.g., 'Too risky for our portfolio')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Update state machine: PILOT → FEEDBACK. Do NOT delete the package — feed the rejection reason into next iteration. The reason may indicate a fixable problem (e.g., 'too risky' might be addressable by adding independent validation).
examples: Too risky for our portfolio — we only acquire validated products
P-09 is too research-stage for us — come back when molecule is designed
P-04 enzyme engineering is outside our capability — we don't have a bio team

feedback_categories.description: Buyer suggests an alternative use case not in our original TTP (e.g., 'Could this be used for spinal cord injury patients?')
feedback_categories.machine_action: Evaluate alternative use case. If viable, may create a new package (P-16, P-17, etc.) or expand existing package scope.
examples: Could P-01 be used for spinal cord injury patients with multi-level drainage?
Could P-09 be used for glucose monitoring instead of ICP?
Could P-04 be used for non-NPH amyloid clearance (e.g., early AD)?

the_loop: Discovery → Collision → TTP → Buyer Outreach → Buyer Feedback (this schema) → TTP Update → Next Version → Buyer Outreach (re-enter loop)
